title: Understanding Proper Drainage Fall and Slope
description: Achieving correct slope in drainage systems is fundamental to ensuring that wastewater and solid waste are carried smoothly out of the building without leaving residue behind. If a horizontal drainage pipe is pitched too steeply, the liquid water rushes past the solid waste too quickly, leaving the solids stranded in the pipe and eventually forming a blockage. Conversely, if the pipe lacks adequate fall, the water velocity drops, causing sediment to settle out over time. Professional installers rely on established local building codes and precise leveling tools to maintain the correct gradient for every specific pipe size and material type used on the job site.

Understanding Proper Drainage Fall and Slope

Achieving correct slope in drainage systems is fundamental to ensuring that wastewater and solid waste are carried smoothly out of the building without leaving residue behind. If a horizontal drainage pipe is pitched too steeply, the liquid water rushes past the solid waste too quickly, leaving the solids stranded in the pipe and eventually forming a blockage. Conversely, if the pipe lacks adequate fall, the water velocity drops, causing sediment to settle out over time. Professional installers rely on established local building codes and precise leveling tools to maintain the correct gradient for every specific pipe size and material type used on the job site.
